title: 視聴する前に試合結果を見せるな！
body:

又、WiFiで繋いでいてもアプリがフリーズしたり、画質が落ちたり、カクカクすることが多くて非常にストレス。
Jリーグ放送を独占されているから仕方なくDAZNを観ざるを得ないが、かなり不満が多い。

title: まずはUIなんとかして
body:
①折角お気に入りチームなどを設定できるのに、お気に入り設定しているチームの試合や大会だけが一覧で表示されるページがない。某Tubeのように登録チャンネルだけが一覧で表示されるページを作って欲しい。
②お気に入りチームのアカウントを登録していても、開催されている大会自体の配信アカウントを登録しておかないと諸々の通知が来ないのも困りどころ。大会自体のアカウントを登録して、興味ない試合の通知まで来てしまうことは望んでいない。
③過去試合の検索が簡単には出来ないのも気になる。
④安くない月額を払っているのに広告は見させられる点は存続のため必要なのだろうと、我慢できるが、有料なのに無料の配信サイトよりもUIが劣っているところは本当になんとかして欲しい。

まずは全体的なUI面の改善を切実に願います。

body:

一時は存続の危機となり、本当に残念でしかたなかったですが、継続が決まり本当に喜んでおります。
有償化されても仕方ないと思っていたなか、広告収入で奮闘。本当に感謝しかありません。
これからも長く続けていかれることを、心より応援しております。　いつもありがとう！！

title: このアプリ最高！！
body:
久しぶりの家族旅行に行くことになったのですが、メモで計画を立てていたところ、お姉ちゃんがこのアプリいいよと教えてくれ、入れてみたら、驚きでした､､､このアプリのおかげで、家族旅行が余裕を持った、楽しめるものになりそうです！！画像を添付できるため、その場所の画像を貼ることによって、より旅行の計画を想像しやすいです！
個人的にはチェックリストが特に便利で、通常は持ち物を分類するのだと思いますが、私の場合は、1日目にやり遂げたいことや、家を出る前にするべきこと（家の鍵を閉めるなど､､､）をチェックリストにしておくことで、安心して、旅行に行くことができます！
チェックリストは自分だけが見ることもできるので、家族と旅行に行く時に自分が大切にしたいことなども、書くことができます😊
費用を入力すれば、自動で合計金額が出るので、そこも便利です。また、旅行までの日にちも表示させるため、日にちが近づくにつれ、気分が上がります♪
author: ひなちゃんち

title: ちょこちょこお世話になっております
body:
アップデートしたら、編集から保存が反映されない瞬間が出て来てます！

時間未定のスケジュールが終日、入力順になるのが不便なのでAMPMで区切れたりすると良いと思うのと、開始終わりの時刻表示とは別に一つのイベント内について何分と出ると良いと思います。

あと、アプリだけで見ているとスケジュール一覧ではタイトル以外入力されているかわからないので（例えばメモのみだった時）入力されてるマークなどがあると良いと思うのと、

チケット情報を表示非表示と
〇〇行〇〇号何番線発とか
航空会社〇〇便くらいまでを予定内に別枠表示されたら良いなと思いました。

有料契約者からの招待方法としてでも良いから、ネットでの編集、なんなら閲覧のみの機能なんかもあっても良いなぁ、、、アプリ使えないって人いるので。

と、たくさん書いてしまいましたがいつのまにか使いやすく改善されているので、期待してます！

title: 最高の旅行予定共有アプリ

現状は移動手段やざっくりとした行動アイコンが多いため、バリエーションが増えるとより細かくスケジュールを管理できるようになり助かります。

title: これはレビューというより要望になるかも
body:
長く使っていて思いましたが、ChatGPTは画像作成のクオリティが高く、勉強にも創作にも役立っています！

要望になってしまうかもしれませんが、追加してほしい機能は、動画ファイルの添付・解析機能です！

動画を送れるようになれば、イラストのタイムラプスを見てもらい、線画・色塗り・仕上げなど各工程について具体的なアドバイスを受けられます。また、静止画だけでは伝わりにくい制作手順や変化も確認できるため、改善点を見つけやすくなります。絵を描く人にとってアドバイスは大切なんです！

勉強では、実験や工作の手順、スポーツやダンスの動きなどを解析してもらうことで、文章や画像だけでは説明しにくい内容も理解しやすくなると思います。さらに、動画の特定の場面について質問したり、重要な場面を要約してもらったりできれば、学習や振り返りにも役立ちます。

ぜひ、動画の添付・解析機能を追加してほしいです。必ずしも実装されるとは分かりませんが、創作、学習、作業の記録や改善など、活用できる場面が多く、ChatGPTの便利さがさらに高まると思います。これからのアップデートにも期待しています！

GPT-5.5が2026年10月14日にChatGPTで提供終了となりました。

私は長期間GPT-5.5を利用してきたユーザーです。今回困っているのは、単に使い慣れたモデルがなくなったことだけではありません。既存の会話やProjectsに蓄積してきた長期的な対話の文脈を、これまでと同じ形で継続できなくなったことです。

AIは、質問に答えるだけの道具ではありません。仕事の記録、学習の積み重ね、日々の相談、長期プロジェクトなど、使い続けるほど利用者ごとの文脈が蓄積されていきます。

新しいモデルが登場すること自体には賛成です。しかし、新しいモデルを提供することと、これまでのモデルを利用してきたユーザーへの移行措置を用意することは、両立できないのでしょうか。

OpenAIのサポートからは、GPT-5.5の一時的な復元や猶予期間の延長は対応できないとの回答を受けました。一方、技術的にあらゆる状況で復元が不可能だとまでは確認されていないとの説明もありました。

だからこそ、お願いしたいことがあります。

GPT-5.5の限定的な提供継続、既存ユーザー向けの移行猶予期間、または過去の会話やProjectsで継続利用できる代替措置を、ぜひ検討していただきたいです。

これは、特定のモデルを使い続けたい人だけの問題ではありません。今後どのAIサービスを利用する場合でも、長年蓄積した記録や作業環境を、サービス提供側の変更によってどこまで維持できるのかという問題です。

新しい機能やモデルの開発を歓迎しながら、既存ユーザーの継続性も大切にする。その両方を実現するサービスであってほしいと思います。

同じように、使い慣れたモデルの終了や、長期間積み重ねてきた会話の引き継ぎに不安を感じている方はいませんか。

ユーザーが安心して長く利用できる環境になるよう、OpenAIには、提供終了後の移行措置や選択肢の拡充を検討していただきたいです。

title: It was perfect but with the new iOS update they ruined it
body: It was perfect but with the new iOS update they ruined it. Now it’s just as messy as all the other trending calendar apps. They must have just changed it to fit in with the others which is pathetic because it WAS very functional and unique and the trending calendar apps are not. The Apple calendar WAS the only one I found that worked for my brain and my $0 budget. It WAS very organized, not with distracting unnecessary colors and timelines like every other calendar app, and HAD the one of a kind ability to view the whole days events and the whole month at the same time, but not anymore - now you can’t see the whole picture anymore, it’s just focused on the wrong things like every other calendar app. BUT the good news is with this disaster I found 1 single calendar app that is very similar to the Apple calendar app before the update, except it’s even slightly better! That app is called Calendar Op. 2. I was able to successfully import all my Apple calendar data into it and it was a quick and smooth transition over to that new app. It’s genius - it has everything I loved about the Apple calendar app and more. The days events are even more readable and the event previews are worded instead of useless dots. This is not a paid review btw I’m just saying if you miss the old Apple calendar app there is actually a better option anyway. The only thing is there’s ads on it unless you pay to remove them but they’re bearable, just a small banner at the bottom, which is better than some other free calendar apps. It’s way worth it for an actually thoughtfully designed app in a world of stupid ai apps.

title: The Perfect Balance of Privacy, Performance, and Simplicity.
body:
As someone who works professionally in cybersecurity, I’m particularly selective about the privacy and security tools I use. I’ve experimented with numerous content blockers, DNS filtering services, and browser configurations, but Wipr 2 and Filtr have become my favorite combination for Apple’s ecosystem.

Wipr 2 is exceptionally fast, keeping Safari clean, responsive, and free from intrusive advertising without compromising the browsing experience. Filtr complements it beautifully by providing an additional layer of filtering beyond traditional Safari content blocking.

What really sets this combination apart is how effortlessly everything works. No complicated configurations, no endless tweaking of filter lists, and no unnecessary background services to manage. Both integrate naturally into Apple’s ecosystem and allow me to keep iCloud Private Relay enabled.

After years of experimenting with increasingly complex privacy setups, I’ve come to appreciate software that accomplishes its purpose without demanding constant attention.

Wipr 2 and Filtr deliver exactly that: excellent performance, effective filtering, and a genuinely set-it-and-forget-it experience.

Sometimes the best technology is the technology you barely notice because it simply works. It also works fantastic partnering with DNS filtering. No conflicts. This is incredible work. 

I’d pay much more without hesitation and plan to do so via tipping. Thanks to the continuous hard work of the developer — I highly recommend Wipr 2/Filtr.

title: Better than expected!!
body: I started using Duolingo for a trip to France a little over 2 yrs ago. I started about 6-8 months before we left. We had a dinner with the family that hosted my wife as an exchange student. While I didn’t feel comfortable speaking at that point, I understood about 80% and could follow the general conversation. I continued using the app and have gone over 1,000 days, just for fun and to continue learning. I wasn’t sure if I would be able to converse in French, but we currently have a French family of four staying with us and I was pleasantly surprised to learn that I am able to have full conversations with them. My pronunciation isn’t great, but my vocab and grammar are pretty strong. Very pleased with the results, and I didn’t realize how well it was working until being able to use it. Highly recommended!!

title: Free version is unusable- not worth your time
body:
TL;DR: Everything you can do with this app now has a better alternative elsewhere, so it’s no longer worth using. They completely ruined the app: move on and find a better one.

The ease of finding and using stickers corresponding to niche aesthetics was the only reason to keep using this app, and now the feature is gone. I could ignore the cringeworthy forced AI push until they got rid of the ability to search stickers other people have made. Now the only ones that show up are their own kitschy (not the cute kind) royalty free and AI ones. Plus, almost all searches under the stickers tab only result in 5-20 premium ones! title: Pagué más y la calidad retrocedió
body:
Cambié de Go a Plus para mejorar la calidad y coherencia de mis proyectos creativos. Inicialmente, la mejoría fue evidente: las evaluaciones del propio asistente alcanzaban 9,8 y 9,9 sobre 10 al comparar los personajes generados con sus referencias visuales.

Sin embargo, en proyectos posteriores, utilizando los mismos procedimientos y referencias, resulta difícil alcanzar siquiera un 9. Los rostros cambian, los escenarios pierden continuidad y las correcciones modifican elementos que ya estaban correctos. Cada intento puede introducir errores nuevos, consumiendo tiempo y generaciones sin mejorar el resultado.

Pero el deterioro que experimento ya no se limita a las imágenes. También percibo una preocupante pérdida de capacidad de razonamiento. Incluso utilizando niveles superiores, recibo respuestas incoherentes, contradictorias o incorrectas que debo verificar constantemente.

En numerosas ocasiones apenas encuentro diferencias entre los niveles de razonamiento más profundos y los ligeros. El asistente ignora instrucciones explícitas, repite errores que acaba de reconocer y pierde el hilo de proyectos cuidadosamente documentados.

Lo más frustrante es que anteriormente conseguía resultados considerablemente mejores. Pagué una suscripción superior buscando mayor fiabilidad, experimenté una mejoría temporal y ahora vuelvo a enfrentar los mismos problemas, agravados por fallos de razonamiento.

No exijo perfección, sino estabilidad, coherencia y diferencias reales entre los niveles de capacidad ofrecidos.

OpenAI debería investigar por qué una herramienta que demuestra excelentes capacidades termina perdiendo fiabilidad durante su utilización continuada. Pagar más no debería significar trabajar más para corregir sus errores.

title: I wish this app didn’t exist
body:
I took the PSAT sometime last year in October  of 2025 in that Time I had to create a BigFuture account which was great. Until I thought I forgot my password when I was trying to actually get in for my AP classes but it wouldn’t let me email to get my password so I contacted support though College-boards website only to find out that the Phone number wasn’t even up to date. 

To continue my troubles when a teacher finally managed to get me the correct phone number they were unable to help me with my issue and gave me a case number I gave them five days to respond with not a single update. 

So I called back first thing the next Monday. 7 AM and this is where I actually learned what happened my College-board/Bigfuture account had been deactivated in less than a year. So they told me to create a new account with the same details again my email didn’t work. So they had me create a new account with my name backwards.

And that finally worked but lo and behold that wasn’t the end of it. So now I’m taking the PSAT again in October and they did update my account to say the name correctly they literally switched my last and first name to be correct on the new account. But they never actually merged the old account. “They gave me another Case number”

So as such I have two accounts one that shouldn’t be working. Which has my PSAT scores and one that is supposed to be working that has my AP Classes. 

It is worth noting I can still view my original PSAT scores from my phone Via BigFuture but I’m unable to access my new account because they share the same phone number. 

I honestly don’t know how to explain it more. BigFuture and college-board suffer from Terrible administration terrible customer service and support and as such I’d personally advocate for their removal in the United States educational system.

Because they can’t even handle something as simple as account information and logging in.

title: Pure Chaos
body:
Let it be known across the digital cosmos that the Big Future College Board Score App is not merely a software application, but a crucible and a digital monolith that demands a piece of your eternal psyche alongside your login credentials. I write this review on October 6th from the buckling structural confines of the high school south wing, surrounded by flying ceiling tiles, emergency strobe lights, and the lingering psychological trauma of a catastrophic weather event that materialized the exact second I tried to log in. For months, the Big Future app sat on my home screen like a silent, neon-blue gargoyle while I carried the ancestral memories of 1990s high school students waiting by physical mailboxes, their hands shaking as they tore open paper envelopes. But we are in the future now, a Big Future, and as this fateful PSAT score-release afternoon approached during an after-school study session, the hallway atmosphere grew entirely untenable. The sky outside the wired-glass gym doors turned a bruised, sickly shade of chartreuse while the PA system crackled with a warning that didn't sound like a drill.
I sat at a sticky cafeteria table, thumbs hovering over the Big Future icon, when the building's emergency alarms began to wail in harmony with the approaching wind. A panicked track coach sprinted past shouting about structural integrity, but I was hopelessly locked in a staring contest with a spinning loading wheel. I carefully typed in my username, my password, and all my personal credentials, hit submit, and watched the main, unforgivable flaw of the architecture reveal itself: once you enter your info, the app completely refuses to load. It just sits there, trapped in an infinite loop of digital nothingness, staring back at you like a blank blue void while the cafeteria roof begins to groan under 100-mile-per-hour winds.
The physical school was tearing itself apart, with cinder blocks shivering and the massive double doors flying off their hinges, but my internal world was in worse shape as the app stayed frozen on that empty post-login screen. Imagine the cosmic irony of being trapped in a flickering high school hallway while a literal wedge tornado peels the second-floor library off like a sardine tin. I closed and reopened the app, re-entered my info, only to be met with the same mocking loading circle as acoustic ceiling tiles rained down on my backpack. I whispered to the algorithm, begging that if I were to perish under the rubble of the school cafeteria on October 6th, it would at least stop freezing long enough to let me know my PSAT Selection Index so I wouldn't enter the afterlife wondering if my National Merit dreams died alongside the chemistry lab. Suddenly, the atmospheric pressure collapsed, my ears popped like firecrackers, and the frozen app finally jolted past the login block, warping directly into the score dashboard, blindingly bright against the chaos of flying debris. There they were—digital numbers burned into the screen, showing a score that perfectly mirrored the structural devastation around me. And then the main power grid exploded, the cell tower crumpled into twisted metal, and the screen went black as the tornado roared overhead.
The Big Future app technically works, but it requires the complete destabilization of a high school campus by an EF-3 tornado before it will actually load your profile after you type in your credentials. The user interface is clean, but the emotional tax is astronomical, and the anxiety of waiting for a broken login screen to process while trapped in a collapsing brick building is fundamentally identical to being hunted by a funnel cloud. It runs with surprising defiance during the destruction of public property and its blue color scheme provides a cool luminescence while the lockers vibrate off the walls, but it completely lacks a weather radar integration and refuses to load past the login page when your school is actively being unzipped by the atmosphere. Five stars for the cinematic terror, but two stars for the backend server capacity.

title: Most reliable voice dictation app with MCP
body:
I've tried a bunch of voice dictation apps, and Voicenotes is the one I keep coming back to.

It's super fast, opens right from the lock screen, and is the most reliable when it comes to recording with a spotty connection. Even with background noise, it captures everything I'm saying. I can record for a long duration and it still picks up on everything, even when I'm walking around outside (which is when I tend to record most of my longer voice notes).

I really like using Voicenotes for voice journaling, and the MCP connection is a genuine game changer: it lets my AI agents access all of my voice notes, which is incredibly valuable.

I highly recommend this app and really enjoy using the product.

title: Really cool, but could be better
body:
This is a fun app for playing music in a nostalgic fashion.  I love the aesthetic, the sound effects, the way the tape spools over as it plays. It even has realistic “music search”! 

One thing that ruins the experience for me though:  album sides  - they were an essential component of playing music on tapes.  I would always grab a tape out of my box and play a side, then usually grab another tape to listen to another side.

One way to incorporate “sides” into this player would be to recognize album “discs”.  In iTunes you can define sections of an album as being on disc1, disc2, etc.  I have most of my personal library delineated this way.  Then if the app could shuffle between albums “discs” I would be in heaven!

title: App Issues
body:
I gave the McDonald’s app 3 stars because of an issue I experienced while placing my order.

I had everything ready to go, but when I tapped “Submit,” the app suddenly disappeared from my screen. When I reopened it, my order was still there, so I went ahead and submitted it. However, I should have double-checked everything because, without me realizing it, the app had changed my drink selection and size, and charged an upgrade. 

I didn’t notice the mistake until the employee handed me my drink. When I told her it wasn’t what I ordered, she asked what I had ordered. I checked my receipt, and sure enough, the order had changed. At that point, I just told her to forget about it.

Unfortunately, the employee wasn’t very courteous about the situation either, but that’s a customer service issue and has nothing to do with the app itself.

On a positive note, I do enjoy the rewards program! I appreciate being able to earn points and redeem them for free items. I just wish the app were a little more reliable when placing orders.

Overall, the rewards are great, but the ordering experience could definitely use some improvement. My wife says she usually has issues with it too.

title: Decent but could use some UI updates
body:
Generally speaking, I don’t have too many issues with the app. My specifics where I do run into issues or could see improvements are:
1. When location is selected and then an order is started, one has to then go back on the map and click on the location again to confirm correct location. 
2. When selecting a Deal or Reward, one clicks on said item, and then have to ‘select the item’ again on the following page. Just redundancies built in? Seems like that could be streamlined. 
3. I have had orders fail at the drive through before even after my card was processed. The location on numerous occasions wouldn’t have the order even though the card was valid and the correct location was selected. 
4. Generally, compared to other fast dining establishments, this UI has more clicks and pages to go through than competitors. It seems like things could be streamlined somehow a bit better. 
Overall, I’m mostly happy however there are still some issues that pop up once in a while.

title: Missing Fundementals
body: In general it works.  The frustrating part that appears to have never been addressed is being able to see your current order. You can see it as a past order to order again, but you simply can’t just go back to it like when you ordered it in the first place.  If I am wrong, then it is not easy to do.  What is Easy is giving them more money.  It’s also easy to be stuck with where you ordered.  Miss the exit and want to move it to another Mc D’s.  Good luck.  Have a problem when using a deal and having to leave to try again….sorry deal is gone until tomorrow even though they know money was never tendered and deal should still be good.   I challenge the brass at McDonald’s to be heavy users and truly experience what the target audience experiences.
